archetype.name: Pocket Passer (play-action distributor)
archetype.definition: Goff wins from a clean, well-timed pocket by throwing on rhythm to a deep stable of targets. He offers almost nothing as a runner, and this year he is pushing the ball into tighter windows downfield more often than he ever has in Detroit.

report.headline: Same Goff, more aggressive: the downfield gains are real, the turnover luck isn't
report.take:
Goff is what he has been for most of the Detroit years: a top-ten efficiency passer who lives on timing, a strong supporting cast and a clean pocket. His 0.266 EPA per dropback ranks 9th of 47, and his 10 passing EPA per game ranks 4th. He is 1.97 adjusted net yards per dropback above the league average. None of that is out of character. The 2024 and 2025 lines sit in the same neighborhood, and the 7.92 yards per attempt is almost exactly last year's 7.9.

What has changed is the shape of the throws. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, is 18.55%, up 6.1 points on last season and well above the 11-13% band he has lived in since 2020. His intended air yards of 8.17 are also longer than his recent career aDOTs. That is where the production comes from. Throws of 10+ air yards are averaging 0.913 EPA, and the intermediate band alone has added 50.9 EPA, most of his passing value. Everything under 10 yards is merely solid at 0.106, and the screens and swings behind the line are a drag. The 20-attempt deep split, with a 13.1 CPOE, is a hint rather than a fact. The intermediate work is a big enough sample to take seriously.

The numbers flatter him in two places. One interception on 248 attempts, a 0.4% rate ranked 7th, is not who he is. He threw 8 last year and 12 in 2024, and the riskier target profile should push picks up, not down. Six turnover-worthy fumbles also suggest the lone fumble lost is fortunate. The other weak spot is the money down. On third down he is at -0.175 EPA with a -9.7 CPOE and 6 of his 16 sacks, converting 34.8% while facing 7.5 yards to go on average. That is the soft spot in an otherwise excellent profile.

The recent stretch reads as steady rather than slipping. Over his last three games, yards per attempt is up and the team is 3-0, but volume fell to 29 attempts a game and the sack rate rose to 8.4%. Much of that comes from one game: the Week 8 grind against Minnesota, now the league's top-ranked defense, where he was sacked 4 times and finished at -4.2 EPA. A Lions offense that passes less than expected and a defense ranked 30th by EPA keep his game scripts busy either way. He has thrived when chasing, at 0.418 EPA when trailing by 9 or more.

strengths.title: Intermediate and downfield efficiency
strengths.body: His value is concentrated in throws of 10+ air yards, which average 0.913 EPA. That is driven by an intermediate band that has added 50.9 EPA on 61 attempts. It fits a real change in approach, with tight-window throws up sharply from last season, rather than a fluky handful of bombs. The intermediate production should hold. The deep split is too small to bank on at this level.

strengths.title: Top-tier per-play value, sustained for years
strengths.body: He ranks 9th in EPA per dropback and 4th in passing EPA per game. The career log shows top-16 efficiency in every season since 2022. This is the product of a stable system and cast rather than a hot month, so it is the most bankable part of his profile.

strengths.title: LaPorta as the efficiency engine
strengths.body: Sam LaPorta's 0.738 EPA per target is the best among his main receivers. Goff's best work in the middle-depth range runs through the tight end and Jameson Williams more than through Amon-Ra St. Brown's volume. Having several plus options means one bracketed receiver doesn't sink the passing game.

concerns.title: Third down is a real hole
concerns.body: His third-down plays come in at -0.175 EPA with a -9.7 CPOE. They also account for six of his sacks, and Detroit converts only 34.8%. Facing 7.5 yards to go on average explains part of it, but the accuracy drop is his own. It is the main thing separating him from the very top of the position, and it has not fixed itself as the season has gone on.

concerns.title: Interception rate will regress
concerns.body: A 0.4% interception rate is far below anything in his career: 8 picks last year, 12 in 2024, and a two-interception full-season pace now. Pairing that with a much more aggressive target profile and six turnover-worthy fumbles points to turnovers arriving later in the season. This is luck, not a new skill.

concerns.title: Sacks creeping up lately
concerns.body: He is pressured on only 16.2% of dropbacks, 6th-lowest. But when pressure arrives it turns into sacks 28.6% of the time, a bit worse than his career norm. His recent sack rate is 2.4 points above his season mark. Much of that came against Minnesota's top-ranked defense, but a questionable starting center makes it worth tracking.

trend.note: His efficiency has held in a narrow band all year, with yards per attempt actually up over the last three games. The one real dip was Week 8 against Minnesota's No. 1 defense, not a slide, though attempts have dropped as Detroit has led more.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense in football, with a TE-shaped hole
nextGame.body:
Miami ranks 32nd in pass EPA allowed and 32nd in success rate allowed, and 30th in deep EPA allowed. That last one lines up directly with Goff's 10+ air-yard profile. Quarterbacks are scoring 2.57 touchdowns a game against Miami, 30th, and the 27th-ranked sack rate should give his line an easier afternoon than Minnesota did. The one place Miami has held up is against opposing WR1s, at 7.5 PPR under their averages, 2nd. That suggests the yardage tilts toward LaPorta, Williams and the backs rather than St. Brown. Detroit is a 7-point favorite with a 50.5 total. Miami's offense ranks 23rd in EPA and runs far more than expected, so a comfortable lead could cap his volume late, as it did in recent weeks.

The availability that matters is in the middle of his line. Center Cade Mays is questionable with a low ankle sprain from the Minnesota game. A shaky interior is the most likely way his recent sack uptick continues, though Miami's weak rush blunts the risk. On Miami's side, starting tackle Kadyn Proctor is out, which hurts their offense more than their defense. That nudges the game script toward a Detroit lead. Rotational end Malik Herring, questionable, plays about a third of the snaps and moves little.

keyMatchups.title: LaPorta against Miami's tight-end coverage
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows 0.89 EPA per target to opposing top tight ends, worst in the league, and sends opponents a larger share of TE targets than the league norm. LaPorta is already Goff's most efficient target. The seam and intermediate middle should be open all day.

keyMatchups.title: His downfield game against a leaky secondary
keyMatchups.body: Goff's throws of 10+ air yards average 0.913 EPA, and Miami is 30th in deep EPA allowed and dead last in pass EPA allowed. If he keeps his more aggressive approach, this is where the big plays come from.

keyMatchups.title: Game script and passing volume
keyMatchups.body: Detroit already passes less than expected, ranking 25th in pass rate over expected, and Miami's offense is unlikely to force a shootout. A lead could leave Goff on the low-30s attempt count of recent weeks. That makes efficiency, not volume, his path to a big line.

nextGame.watch: Whether Mays plays at center, and whether the third-down sacks from the Minnesota game carry over against a much weaker rush.

restOfSeason.body:
The core should hold: top-ten efficiency, strong yardage per attempt, and touchdown production from a red-zone offense where he has 12 scores. That is backed by the same system and receivers that produced his 2024-25 seasons. Expect roughly 255 to 290 passing yards and around two touchdowns a game. Volume may sit slightly below his early-season attempt counts while Detroit leads and leans on the run.

Two things should regress. Interceptions will come back toward his career norms given how often he is throwing into tight windows; something like 0.3 to 0.7 a game is more realistic than the near-zero so far. The deep-ball efficiency, on just 20 attempts, will cool. Third down is the swing skill: even modest improvement there would offset the turnover regression. Detroit's 30th-ranked defense keeps the door open for high-volume shootouts, and he has been at his best when trailing.
swingFactors: Interior line health with Mays hurt
Whether the tight-window aggressiveness keeps paying off or turns into picks
How often Detroit's porous defense forces him to throw

confidence.note: Seven games, but the profile matches his multi-year baseline. The interception rate and deep split rest on small samples.
